---
title: Local monitored sampling
---

Install with `pip install pymc-monitor` or `pip install pymc-monitor[nutpie,notebook]`.
No Modal account, remote worker, or cache is needed.

## Quick start

This tiny example runs during the documentation build and checks the report.

```{python}
import pymc as pm
import pymc_monitor as monitor

with pm.Model() as model:
    mu = pm.Normal("mu")
    pm.Normal("y", mu, observed=[0.2, -0.1])

idata = monitor.sample(model=model, draws=8, tune=8, chains=2, cores=1, progress=False)
report = monitor.read_report(idata)
assert report["draws"] == 8
print(report["status"], report["draws"])
```

## Targets

`until="final"` requires effective sample size 400, auto-scaled R-hat, zero
post-warmup divergences, and BFMI >= 0.3. `until="draft"` uses ESS 100 and
R-hat <= 1.05. For custom policy use a dictionary such as
`until={"preset": "draft", "ess": 200, "patience": 3, "escalate": 1}`.
`until=None` still attaches a display-only diagnostic report. Missing required
HMC statistics fail closed. Every element of every free variable is assessed.
Constrained samples are used for live diagnostics even when PyMC stores a
transformed sampling value internally. Nested R-hat requires `superchains` to
divide the total chain count.

## Control and events

Call `start(...)` to get a `SamplingHandle`: `wait(timeout=None)` returns
InferenceData, `stop()` requests cancellation, `snapshot()` returns current
state, `done` indicates completion, `close()` releases the dashboard and joins
the run. If no complete post-warmup draw can be recovered on stop,
`SamplingStoppedError` is raised. JAX samplers support phase-only progress and
cannot stop early; adaptive `until` with JAX raises. Nutpie supports native
`inspect()` checkpoints and `abort()` on stop. Pass `on_event` to receive typed
phase, per-chain, and convergence updates, or use `iter_sample` directly.

`dashboard=True` serves a per-run authenticated HTTP dashboard on
`127.0.0.1`, with a bearer token in the URL fragment. The server rejects
unauthorized state and stop requests and does not fetch third-party assets.
Call `close()` when done with the dashboard. The `DashboardState` reducer and
static HTML/JS/CSS are reusable by a remote consumer without importing its
transport into this package.
